_note: Sidecar for the Norwegian Getaway Aug 24 2026 itinerary-change news article. Primary source is the operator-supplied NCL guest notification (three screenshots of the email, received in the operator's inbox, provided in-session 2026-08-22). Secondary corroboration verified in-session via WebSearch + WebFetch. GSC waterpark timing from household memory b4e7d905, whose SSOT is admin/sources/ncl-gsc-great-tides-waterpark/gsc-booklet-extracted-text.txt in this repo. No affiliate links (news piece; nothing to sell).

revised_itinerary.claim: Aug 24 2026 Miami sailing: Mon Miami overnight; Tue depart 3:00 am, arrive Nassau 7:30 pm (overnight); Wed Nassau depart 11:59 pm; Thu Great Stirrup Cay 8:00 am - 8:00 pm; Fri Miami 7:00 am. Original: Wed Nassau 8-5, Thu GSC 8-5.
revised_itinerary.source: NCL guest notification email, original-vs-revised tables (operator screenshots, 2026-08-22) — PRIMARY
revised_itinerary.derived_durations: Article's duration figures are arithmetic on the letter's times, stated with the times attached in-text per Sophos fabricated_duration finding 2026-08-22: original Nassau call 8:00 am - 5:00 pm = 9h; revised alongside 7:30 pm Tue - 11:59 pm Wed = 28h29m, stated as 'about 28½ hours'. 'Roughly triples' in summaries = 28.5/9 ≈ 3.2x.

reason_technical_issue.claim: NCL: ship 'experienced a technical issue that requires additional time in Nassau, Bahamas to complete the necessary repairs'; 'does not affect the safety of the vessel'; 'additional time alongside is required'
reason_technical_issue.source: NCL letter verbatim (operator screenshots) — PRIMARY. Matching phrasing quoted by Cruise Hive.

propulsion_component.claim: The technical issue is a propulsion component; ship sailed at reduced speed during the repair period
propulsion_component.source: https://www.cruisehive.com/propulsion-problem-keeps-norwegian-cruise-ship-in-port-until-midnight/214347 (WebFetch 2026-08-22, verbatim: 'a technical issue affecting a propulsion component that requires additional time in Nassau, Bahamas to complete the necessary repairs'; reduced sailing speed noted) — SECONDARY, attributed in-article as 'cruise media report'
propulsion_component.notes: The guest letter never names the system; the article says so explicitly and attributes the propulsion identification to cruise media, not NCL.

july_31_precedent.claim: The July 31, 2026 three-night sailing had its Nassau call extended from 5:00 pm to 11:59 pm (nearly 7 extra hours) for the same repairs
july_31_precedent.source: Cruise Hive (same article, WebFetch 2026-08-22) + https://www.cruisemummy.co.uk/propulsion-repairs-force-norwegian-getaway-into-extended-nassau-stay/ (search result corroboration)

miami_overnight_shore_power.claim: The Miami overnight + 3:00 am Tuesday departure supports shore power system testing at PortMiami and is unrelated to the propulsion repairs
miami_overnight_shore_power.source: Cruise Hive (WebFetch 2026-08-22: 'The ship will remain docked overnight in Miami to assist the port with shore power system tests. This itinerary change is unrelated to the propulsion repairs.') — SECONDARY, attributed as 'cruise media report'

casino_shops_closed_alongside.claim: Casino and onboard retail close while docked (in-port rules); reported during the Aug 1 extended Nassau call
casino_shops_closed_alongside.source: Cruise Hive (WebFetch 2026-08-22: 'Retail stores and casino must close while docked; other onboard operations continue normally') + standard industry practice in Bahamian ports

gsc_waterpark_september.claim: Great Tides Waterpark at Great Stirrup Cay is slated to open September 2026 — after this sailing; access bookable via NCL app, pricing not yet public
gsc_waterpark_september.source: Household memory b4e7d905 (SSOT: admin/sources/ncl-gsc-great-tides-waterpark/gsc-booklet-extracted-text.txt — NCL marketing booklet dated 2026-05-26)
gsc_waterpark_september.notes: Article states only the opening window and that the extended day precedes it; no pricing claimed.

no_compensation_contract.claim: The letter mentions no compensation; cruise contracts permit itinerary changes without compensation; NCL-sold excursions adjust automatically, third-party bookings are the guest's to move
no_compensation_contract.source: Letter (primary — absence of any compensation language); contract point per existing site coverage articles/cruise-itinerary-changes-what-to-do.html; excursion handling is standard NCL practice framed with 'typically / verify in the app' hedge

authorship_note.framing: The dek says the change letter 'landed in my inbox this week' — factual (operator supplied his own received email). The article does NOT claim the author is booked on the sailing, because the operator did not state it. If the operator confirms he is sailing, a one-line booked-on-it strengthener can be added.
authorship_note.quoted_marketing: NCL's 'additional opportunities to soak up the sun' phrasing is quoted once, attributed, and analyzed — not adopted as site voice.

voice_audit.authorship_mode: News analysis of a primary-source document in the operator's possession; calm-authority register per current voice template (articles/caribbean-cruise-trends-2026.html, memory 2b89a833).

machine_tells.notes: NCL's own marketing line appears once inside quotation marks with attribution and critique — quoted material, not site voice. 'exclusive destination' from the letter is NOT quoted anywhere.

must_be_present.honest_limitation_acknowledged: Yes — the letter never names the failed system and the article says so; 'schedule written in pencil' caveat; propulsion identification explicitly attributed to media, not NCL.
must_be_present.real_numbers: Port hours, dates, the ~28-hour Nassau math, 7:30 pm / 11:59 pm / 8 pm times, July 31 precedent.
must_be_present.pastoral_honesty: Names the reader's likely irritation at the marketing wrapping and defuses it rather than stoking it.

voice_audit.risk_rating_justification: Primary-source anchored; secondary claims attributed; no lived-experience overclaim (no booked-on-it assertion without operator confirmation); marketing language quarantined in quotes.
